# AI speak patterns, part 4

Built from the packs in `hooks/lib/patterns`. Each section names its own source.

The category index is in `ai-speak-patterns.md`.

## file-narration

Presets: `ryan`, `technical`, `git`, `all`. Source: Group G research: git commit-message conventions and conventional commits.

Text narrates a trivial file operation instead of stating the change.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `This commit adds` | state the change, cut the frame |
| `This commit introduces` | state the change, cut the frame |
| `This PR introduces` | state the change, cut the frame |
| `This PR adds` | state the change, cut the frame |
| `Here's what changed` | list the changes directly |
| `The file now contains` | state the content directly |
| `Added a new file called` | name the file, cut the frame |
| `I've updated the`, `I've added a` | state the change, cut the frame |
| a line opening with `Updated`, `Added`, or `Deleted` plus a file name | use the imperative mood |

The past-tense form has to open the line, so a conventional-commit subject such as `docs: update README` stays clean.

## praise-sandwich

Presets: `ryan`, `git`, `all`. Source: Group G research: Wikipedia compliment sandwich, Radical Candor feedback sandwich.

Review or reply text opens and closes with praise around a middle critique.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Review or reply text opens and closes with praise around a middle critique. | `minParagraphs = 3`, `minWords = 18` |

Needs praise in the first and last paragraph and a critique marker between them. People are taught this shape too, so the pack stays out of the `default` preset.

## smart-punctuation

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: Group P research: Wikipedia, Signs of AI writing.

Curly quotes and the ellipsis character typical of text pasted from a chat UI.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| a curly double quote | use a straight double quote |
| a curly opening single quote | use a straight single quote |
| a curly apostrophe | use a straight apostrophe |
| an ellipsis character | use three periods |

Prose files stay out of scope on purpose: a whole-file scan re-reports typeset quotes that a person committed once. A project that wants `files` coverage overrides the pack.

## unicode-glyphs

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: Group P research: Wikipedia, Signs of AI writing.

Arrows, box drawing, dingbats, and geometric symbols used in place of plain ASCII or words.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| an arrow character | use `->` or `<-`, or words |
| a box-drawing character | use ASCII table characters |
| a dingbat or check mark | use `[x]`, `[ ]`, or words |
| a miscellaneous symbol | use plain words, drop the symbol |
| a bullet character | use `-` or `*` for list items |
| a geometric shape character | use plain words, drop the symbol |

Every range skips code points that are also `Extended_Pictographic`, so emoji stay with the `formatting` pack and the dash characters stay with `em-dash`. Prose files stay out of scope for the same reason as `smart-punctuation`. Code comments are out of scope too: a measured pass over 797 library files found arrows in JSDoc examples and box-drawing type diagrams in hand-written comments, and the pack cannot tell those from decoration.
